title: [bug] Tauri fails to build on Fedora 41 (Failed to get GBM device)
body:

2. `npm create tauri-app@latest` (Choose default options with React)
3. `npm install`
4. `npm run tauri dev`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
They don't contain the very same error message i think but i'll close this as a duplicate of https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/5143 and https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/9304. We already have too many issues open for "white window" upstream issues imo.
Thanks for the report nonetheless.
Also, webkitgtk released a new version today, so maybe keep your eyes open for that to hit the distro repos.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Are you using Wayland + Nvidia? If so, it has already been reported earlier https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/8254 . Using `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 npm run tauri dev` may be used as a workaround for now.

Also, it can be issue with `webkit2gtk-4.0: 2.42.1` , like reported here https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/7927

It is most probably an upstream issue, as already suggested.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 All my tests were done on VMs with the standard ISO installations.

Thanks so much that actually managed to fix the issue for running, when building on Debian/Ubuntu base so that I can run on Fedora do I have to run it with this argument or can I somehow set it in the configs so that this is done automatically for me?

As for the Fedora webkit version:
`Package "webkit2gtk4.1-2.46.4-1.fc41.x86_64" is already installed.`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
you could add this above the `tauri::Builder` line in lib.rs/main.rs
```rs
std::env::set_var("WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER", "1"); // alternatively `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE` if this one is not enough
```

comments.body:
The explanation is actually quite simple. lib.rs only contains env vars that you'll need when the compiled app is actually running, it does _not_ affect the build environment.
NO_STRIP is an env var for linuxdeploy, a part of the appimage bundler, though so it needs to be set in the terminal session where you run `npm run tauri build` but does _not_ need to be set in lib.rs for the runtime environment.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> so appimage specific logic doesn't seem so far off.

This isn't appimage specific, just allow the thing to be portable, this is already commonly done on most other software without being appimage. 

Applications usually check `XDG_DATA_DIRS` before checking `/usr/share`, the dynamic linker will check `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before searching for libraries elsewhere, Qt itself has `QT_PLUGIN_PATH` available by default and they even provide a different method with a `qt.conf` file that accepts relative paths to avoid setting the env variable.

pipewire as `PIPEWIRE_MODULE_DIR`, mesa has `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_DIRS` and `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH` and the [later was recently dropped](https://<redacted-host>/news/Mesa-24.2-Modern-Interfaces) and the env variable no longer needs to be set, now the `dri` libs are searched like any other shared library without having to set the env variable.
